methodological_rigor.justification: Retrospective single-center case series of 29 PCNSL patients. Authors appropriately avoided Cox proportional hazards regression due to insufficient events per variable, acknowledging this as exploratory analysis. Kaplan-Meier curves with log-rank testing applied. Pre-specified MRI-to-biopsy interval categories (0-7, 8-14, ≥15 days) predefined to reflect clinical thresholds. Standardized HD-MTX-based therapy limits systemic treatment heterogeneity. However, very small sample size (n=29), no multivariable adjustment, and all key associations fail conventional statistical significance (steroid p=0.127, MRI-to-biopsy OS p=0.074, MRI-to-biopsy PFS p=0.095).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Retrospective case series without comparison group (LoE 4). Identifies potentially modifiable early neurosurgical workflow factors in aggressive PCNSL, an understudied rare malignancy. Clinical relevance limited by underpowered exploratory design; no definitive evidence that steroid avoidance or diagnostic acceleration improves outcomes; all associations hypothesis-generating rather than practice-changing.

reporting_quality.justification: Retrospective case series without applicable standard reporting checklist. Methods section clearly describes inclusion/exclusion criteria, workflow interval definitions (pre-biopsy steroid exposure as binary, MRI-to-biopsy intervals, biopsy-to-induction timing), and outcome definitions. Limitations section transparently acknowledges retrospective design, small sample, missing steroid dose/duration data, and heterogeneous treatment regimens. Data availability: no statement regarding data repository access.

novelty_literature.justification: Novel investigation of early neurosurgical workflow factors (pre-biopsy corticosteroid exposure, MRI-to-biopsy diagnostic timing) in PCNSL prognosis. Extends beyond established MSKCC and IELSG prognostic models that emphasize host and treatment factors, instead focusing on modifiable early diagnostic phase under neurosurgical control. Conceptually innovative but limited by underpowered exploratory design.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-structured case series paper establishing clear clinical rationale for investigating neurosurgical workflow decisions in time-sensitive PCNSL. Thoughtful discussion of confounding by indication for steroid exposure (corticosteroid use as marker of clinical severity rather than causal factor). Appropriate caveats throughout emphasizing exploratory nature. MSKCC model validation as internal validity check. Limitations section comprehensive. Publication-ready organization despite underpowered findings.

key_strengths: Identifies potentially modifiable early neurosurgical workflow factors (empiric pre-biopsy corticosteroid avoidance and diagnostic timing urgency) in understudied PCNSL population where conventional prognostic models overlook neurosurgical entrance phase
Demonstrates appropriate statistical judgment by deliberately avoiding Cox regression in small cohort with limited events, acknowledging all associations as exploratory and hypothesis-generating
Includes internal validity check using established MSKCC prognostic model, which shows expected survival discrimination (p=0.038) supporting prognostic model calibration in cohort

Thoughtful discussion of confounding by indication for steroid exposure, recognizing that corticosteroid use may reflect marker of adverse clinical presentation rather than independent causal effect on prognosis
key_concerns: Very small sample size (n=29 total) severely underpowered for robust survival analysis; all key associations fail conventional statistical significance (pre-biopsy steroid p=0.127, MRI-to-biopsy OS p=0.074, MRI-to-biopsy PFS p=0.095)

Retrospective design with incomplete data on steroid dose and duration (analyzed as binary variable); heterogeneous induction regimens and consolidative strategies not adjusted in analysis due to small size

Case series design without comparison cohort or external validation; all findings explicitly acknowledged as exploratory and hypothesis-generating rather than evidence of independent prognostic effects

Biopsy-to-induction interval demonstrates no meaningful association with survival, limiting ability to identify modifiable windows within neurosurgical control; finding may reflect insufficient power rather than true biological neutrality
chief_reviewer.rationale: Hypothesis-generating case series addressing understudied early diagnostic phase in PCNSL, but very small sample size with non-significant associations (p-values 0.074-0.127) and retrospective design limit evidence strength to exploratory tier 4. Appropriate for specialty journals with explicit framing as preliminary findings requiring prospective validation.
